title: The condensed ring $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$
statement:
For a prime $\ell$, the condensed ring $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is the condensed ring
$\underline T$ of [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] for $T=\mathbf Q_\ell$ with the
$\ell$-adic topology:

$$
\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Q_\ell).
$$

Its underlying ring object is commutative. Postcomposition with the inclusion
$\mathbf Z_\ell\subseteq\mathbf Q_\ell$ ([def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map]) gives
the inclusion $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$
([def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring]), a morphism of condensed rings.

proof.text: Use the complete nonarchimedean valued field $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and its absolute value from [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], with metric $d(x,y)=|x-y|_\ell$. The field operations are commutative. Their continuity follows directly from $|(x+y)-(a+b)|_\ell\leq\max(|x-a|_\ell,|y-b|_\ell)$, $|(-x)-(-a)|_\ell=|x-a|_\ell$, and $|xy-ab|_\ell\leq\max(|x-a|_\ell|y|_\ell,|a|_\ell|y-b|_\ell)$. Indeed, if $|y-b|_\ell<1$, then $|y|_\ell\leq M:=\max(1,|b|_\ell)$; for a prescribed $\varepsilon>0$ take both input distances less than $\min(1,\varepsilon/(1+M+|a|_\ell))$. The displayed bounds prove continuity, so $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is a commutative topological ring.

source.place: statement: the prime and the ell-adic topology

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring] to this commutative topological ring. Define $\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ to be the resulting sheaf, whose sections are $C(S,\mathbf Q_\ell)$, whose restrictions are precomposition, and whose operations are pointwise. The same cited statement gives its underlying ring object and its commutativity. This supplies exactly the section-defined condensed ring; no localization construction is used.

source.place: paragraph defining the sections of underline T and the first ell-adic bullet

proof.text: The valuation-ring description in [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] identifies $\mathbf Z_\ell$ with the subring $\{x\in\mathbf Q_\ell:|x|_\ell\leq1\}$. Its inclusion $i$ preserves $0,1,+,\cdot$ because these are restricted field operations. For $x,y\in\mathbf Z_\ell$ and $n\geq0$, put $z=(y-x)/\ell^n$ in $\mathbf Q_\ell$. Since $|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}$, multiplicativity gives $|z|_\ell=\ell^n|y-x|_\ell$; the cited valuation-ring equality therefore gives $y\in x+\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell$ if and only if $|y-x|_\ell\leq\ell^{-n}$. Nonzero absolute values are integral powers of $\ell$, so this closed ball is also the open ball $|y-x|_\ell<\ell^{1-n}$. As $\ell>1$ and $\ell^{-n}\to0$, these balls form a neighborhood basis for the restricted metric. Thus the $\ell$-adic topology on $\mathbf Z_\ell$, defined by the cosets $x+\ell^n\mathbf Z_\ell$, is the subspace topology. Restricting the continuous ring operations of step 1 makes $\mathbf Z_\ell$ a commutative topological ring. Its distance is the restricted distance, so $d(i(x),i(y))=d(x,y)$; the same epsilon proves continuity. Thus $i$ is an injective continuous ring homomorphism.

source.place: last paragraph: the inclusion of the ell-adic integers

proof.text: By [def-sfb-padic-int-condensed-ring], the source sheaf has sections $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell(S)=C(S,\mathbf Z_\ell)$. Apply [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map] to $i$ from step 3: the component on $S$ is $a\mapsto i\circ a$, a morphism of condensed rings with target the sheaf constructed in step 2. It is an inclusion on sections: if $i\circ a=i\circ b$, then injectivity of $i$ gives $a(s)=b(s)$ for every $s$, hence $a=b$. This is precisely the indicated morphism $\underline{\mathbf Z}_\ell\to\underline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
